stories.headline: Allbirds rebrands as Smartbird AI infrastructure firm, hires ex-AWS exec as CEO; shares jump 30%+

key_facts.fact: Allbirds officially renamed itself Smartbird, Inc. on June 17, completing the sale of the Allbirds brand and footwear assets to American Exchange Group and pivoting fully to AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Effective today, Allbirds, Inc. has changed its name to Smartbird, Inc. The company's Class A common stock listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market will continue to trade under the ticker symbol 'BIRD'... The company has completed its previously announced definitive agreement to sell the Allbirds brand and footwear assets.

key_facts.fact: Smartbird appointed Nadia Carlsten — former CEO of DCAI and ex-VP of product at Google spinoff SandboxAQ, who previously launched Amazon's quantum computing service at AWS — as president and CEO.
key_facts.excerpt: While serving as CEO of DCAI, an AI company delivering large-scale GPU compute infrastructure and enterprise AI, [Carlsten] launched a sovereign AI supercomputer in partnership with NVIDIA. As vice president of product at Google spin-off SandboxAQ, Carlsten led the product portfolio across AI, security and hardware platforms. She has also done extensive work on advanced computing platforms, including launching Amazon's quantum computing service during her tenure at Amazon Web Services.

key_facts.fact: Smartbird shares (NASDAQ: BIRD) surged more than 30% on the news (some accounts cited nearly 60%); the stock was up about 25% YTD after Wednesday's move.
key_facts.excerpt: Allbirds changed its name to Smartbird on Wednesday and appointed former Amazon executive Nadia Carlsten as CEO, cementing the former footwear maker's pivot to an AI infrastructure firm and sending its shares up more than 30%.

key_facts.fact: The company strengthened its balance sheet by increasing its convertible financing facility from $50 million to $100 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Smartbird said on Wednesday that it has strengthened its balance sheet by increasing the size of its convertible financing facility from $50 million to $100 million.

key_facts.fact: Smartbird said it provides AI infrastructure as a managed service to save upfront equipment costs for clients and is in active discussions with potential customers, designing its first cluster deployments.
key_facts.excerpt: Smartbird said it provides AI infrastructure as a managed service to save upfront equipment costs for clients. It is in active discussions with potential customers and is designing its first cluster deployments.

key_facts.fact: Joe Vernachio resigned from the company and its board; Lily Yan Hughes was appointed board chair, and Annie Mitchell continues as CFO.
key_facts.excerpt: Carlsten replaces Joe Vernachio, who is resigning from the company and the board of directors. Annie Mitchell will continue to serve as chief financial officer... Lily Yan Hughes, who has served as an independent director of the company since October 2025, has been appointed board chair.

stories.headline: Tim Cook tells WSJ Apple price hikes are 'unavoidable' as AI-driven RAM shortage hits

key_facts.fact: Apple CEO Tim Cook told the Wall Street Journal that price increases for Apple products are 'unavoidable' because rising memory and storage chip costs have become 'unsustainable' to absorb.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Unfortunately, price increases are unavoidable,' said Cook. 'We're doing our best to mitigate the huge increases that are being passed to us, and we've been trying to shield our customers from the increases, but the situation has become unsustainable.'

key_facts.fact: Cook said the price of RAM has more than doubled since October 2025 and likened the memory shortage to a 'hundred-year flood' he hasn't seen in over 40 years.
key_facts.excerpt: The price of Ram - typically one of the cheapest computer components - has more than doubled since October 2025.

key_facts.fact: Research firm TechInsights estimates Apple would need to raise the iPhone 18 Pro price by about $270 to maintain existing profit margins.
key_facts.excerpt: Research firm TechInsights claims Apple will need to make the iPhone 18 Pro around $270 more expensive to keep its existing profit margin.

key_facts.fact: Cook said Apple would use cash reserves to help suppliers expand memory capacity but ruled out building Apple-owned memory or storage manufacturing facilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Cook told the Wall Street Journal that Apple is willing to use its financial resources to help secure memory supply, but he ruled out building Apple-owned memory or storage manufacturing facilities. 'We can't do everything. We know what we're good at,' Cook said.

key_facts.fact: Cook is due to be replaced by John Ternus as Apple's CEO in September after 15 years in the role.
key_facts.excerpt: Cook, who is due to be replaced by John Ternus as Apple's CEO in September after 15 years in the role.

key_facts.fact: Memory chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are prioritizing high-bandwidth memory for AI servers over consumer-device chips, and shortages are expected to persist into 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: While memory chip makers like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are increasing production capacity, much of that added capacity will prioritize server chips. Demand for consumer-device chips is expected to continue to outpace supply.

stories.headline: SpaceX launches first 'stacked' trio of AST SpaceMobile BlueBird direct-to-cell satellites

key_facts.fact: A SpaceX Falcon 9 lifted off from Cape Canaveral SLC-40 at 2:39 a.m. EDT on June 17 carrying BlueBird 8, 9 and 10 — the first time three BlueBirds were stacked in the same fairing.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX launched the BlueBird 8, 9, 10 mission on a Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, lifting off at 2:39 EDT on Wednesday, June 17. AST SpaceMobile confirmed the mission was successful... marking the first mission to stack three BlueBird satellites in the launch fairing.

key_facts.fact: Each Block 2 BlueBird carries a phased-array aperture roughly 2,400 square feet wide, designed to deliver up to ~200 Mbps directly to standard 4G/5G smartphones.
key_facts.excerpt: These satellites will support AST SpaceMobile's cellular broadband network from space. The satellites are designed to deliver peak data speeds of nearly 200 Mbps to standard smartphones, which the company says will provide voice, broadband data, and video from space.

key_facts.fact: AST CEO Abel Avellan said BlueBirds 11-13 will ship shortly for the next launch and units through BlueBird 37 are already in active production at the company's 500,000-sq-ft Midland, Texas facility.
key_facts.excerpt: The next three spacecraft—BlueBirds 11, 12, and 13—are currently undergoing final preparations for shipment to the Florida launch site, while additional units through BlueBird 37 are already in active production and assembly inside the company's 500,000-square-foot facility in Midland, Texas.

key_facts.fact: AST executives told investors they still target 45 BlueBirds in orbit this year despite losing BlueBird 7 to a Blue Origin New Glenn deployment error in late April.
key_facts.excerpt: It faced a recent setback when a Blue Origin New Glenn vehicle deployed its satellite to the wrong orbit in late April. Executives recently told investors they still expect to have 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit this year.

stories.headline: AWS launches Continuum AI security agent and Context knowledge graph at NY Summit, citing Claude Mythos threat

key_facts.fact: AWS unveiled AWS Continuum, a gated-preview AI-native security service that discovers, prioritizes, validates and remediates code vulnerabilities at machine speed
key_facts.excerpt: Introducing AWS Continuum: Security at machine speed— AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities, available in a gated preview, takes findings from across your environment, prioritizes by business impact, proves which are exploitable, and drives a fix through your own process.

key_facts.fact: AWS Continuum was framed as a response to Anthropic's Claude Mythos and Claude Fable models, which can chain software flaws into serious attacks faster than human defenders
key_facts.excerpt: AWS Continuum is the company's response to the release of Anthropic Mythos and Claude Fable, Chet Kapoor, VP of security services and observability at AWS, said during the keynote.

key_facts.fact: AWS also launched AWS Context, a service that automatically builds an organizational knowledge graph from a company's existing data so agents can navigate business rules and domain knowledge at runtime
key_facts.excerpt: AWS Context provides a comprehensive knowledge graph so customers can build agents that know where to get the information they need, provide the right answer or take the right next step, faster.

key_facts.fact: Continuum starts in a supervised 'learn mode' and earns autonomy only as customers grant permission category by category, reflecting AWS's design to maximize agent autonomy while keeping humans in control
key_facts.excerpt: A new security agent, dubbed AWS Continuum, starts in a supervised 'learn mode' and earns the right to act alone only as customers grant it permission, category by category.

key_facts.fact: Amazon S3 now lets customers attach up to 1 GB of mutable, queryable annotations directly to objects, purpose-built for AI agents and autonomous workflows
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon S3 annotations: attach rich, queryable context directly to your objects— Amazon S3 now lets you attach up to 1 GB of rich, mutable, and queryable context directly to your objects using annotations, purpose-built for AI agents and autonomous workflows that need to discover, understand, and act on data at scale without maintaining separate metadata systems.

stories.headline: Blackstone-led group takes Medallia from Thoma Bravo, sealing $5B PE wipeout

key_facts.fact: On June 17 Medallia announced a recapitalization that transfers ownership from Thoma Bravo to an investor group led by Blackstone, Apollo and FS KKR Capital Corp, with the new owners injecting $150M in fresh capital.
key_facts.excerpt: TYSONS, VA – June 17, 2026 – Medallia, the global leader in customer and employee experience, today announced that it has entered into a recapitalization agreement with its lenders that will strengthen its financial foundation for long-term growth. The transaction will significantly reduce Medallia's outstanding debt and provide $150 million of new capital... Medallia will change ownership from Thoma Bravo to an investor group led by Blackstone, Apollo, and FS KKR Capital Corp (FSK).

key_facts.fact: Thoma Bravo will lose the entire $5B it invested in Medallia's 2021 take-private (valued at $6.4B) — described by Verdad Advisers as the second-largest equity wipeout in PE history, behind only TXU.
key_facts.excerpt: Thoma Bravo will lose all of the $5 billion it invested in Medallia when it took the company private in 2021 — a deal valued at $6.4 billion— according to the Financial Times. Only the collapse of Texas utility TXU surpasses it, according to Daniel Rasmussen, a private equity expert at Verdad Advisers who spoke to the Financial Times.

key_facts.fact: The new ownership group were already Medallia's lenders, carrying loans at roughly 60-70 cents on the dollar; Thoma Bravo declined to inject capital when lenders sought more than $500M of additional equity.
key_facts.excerpt: The new ownership group — Blackstone, Apollo and FSK — were already Medallia's lenders and had been carrying those loans at roughly 60 to 70 cents on the dollar, per FT reporting. Thoma Bravo declined to inject additional capital when lenders requested more than $500 million to reduce the debt load over the past year, choosing instead to record what became the largest loss in the firm's 20-year history.

key_facts.fact: Medallia plans to use the new capital plus an existing $500M commitment to accelerate AI-driven product development.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction also advances Medallia's existing $500 million commitment to innovation and AI transformation, the company said.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea warns record Samsung/SK Hynix bonuses risk fueling broader inflation

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Korea's 'Inflation Target Operation Status Review' report released on June 17 warned that exceptional performance bonuses at Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, created by the semiconductor boom, are stimulating wage increase demands across manufacturing and services beyond the IT sector.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bank of Korea analyzed that the exceptional compensation at the two companies, created by the semiconductor boom, is stimulating wage increase demands across manufacturing and service industries beyond the information technology (IT) sector, which could act as upward pressure on consumer prices.

key_facts.fact: Special payments (performance bonuses) in the South Korean IT sector surged 60.6% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026, while wage growth in non-IT sectors was just 2.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Box B of the BOK's 'Inflation Target Operation Status Review' report released on the 17th... special bonuses in the IT sector surged 60.6%, while other wages increased just 2.1%.

key_facts.fact: Securities firms forecast Samsung Electronics' 2026 operating profit at about 350 trillion won ($295 billion) and SK Hynix's at 255 trillion won ($215 billion); Samsung memory division employees could receive average bonuses of 700 million won ($590,000) per person in Q1 2027, while SK Hynix employees receive about 750 million won ($633,000).
key_facts.excerpt: If Samsung Electronics' operating profit reaches approximately 350 trillion won ($295 billion) and SK Hynix's reaches approximately 255 trillion won ($215 billion) this year as securities firms predict, Samsung Electronics memory division employees will receive an average of 700 million won ($590,000) per person in bonuses before tax in the first quarter of next year, while SK Hynix employees will receive approximately 750 million won ($633,000).

key_facts.fact: The BOK found that when bonus increases reach the top 10% of historical levels, fixed monthly pay in other industries rises an additional 0.02-0.03 percentage points, and consumer prices rise by 0.05 percentage points about five months later.
key_facts.excerpt: An analysis of historical data by the BOK found that when bonus increases reached the top 10% of past observations, fixed monthly pay in other industries rose an additional 0.02 to 0.03 percentage point.

key_facts.fact: IT-sector bonuses contributed 1.3 percentage points to Q1 2026's 3.4% nominal wage growth — the 97th percentile of the 2012-2025 distribution — and the BOK projects this could exceed the 99th percentile in early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Nominal wages rose 3.4 percent from a year earlier in the first quarter, with bonuses in the IT sector accounting for 1.3 percentage points of the increase. The contribution ranks in the 97th percentile of the historical distribution from 2012 to 2025... The BOK said the contribution of IT-sector bonuses could exceed the historical 99th percentile early next year, reaching an unprecedented level.

stories.headline: FDA approves AstraZeneca's Truqap as first targeted therapy for PTEN-deficient metastatic prostate cancer

key_facts.fact: On June 17 the FDA approved Truqap (capivasertib) in combination with abiraterone and prednisone for adults with PTEN-deficient metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve/sensitive prostate cancer.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved AstraZeneca's Truqap (capivasertib) in combination with abiraterone and prednisone for adult patients with PTEN-deficient metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve or sensitive (mAPMN/S) prostate cancer. This is the first targeted therapy approved in the United States for this patient population.

key_facts.fact: The FDA simultaneously authorized the VENTANA PTEN (SP218) diagnostic assay to identify eligible patients with PTEN-deficient tumors.
key_facts.excerpt: At the same time, the regulator authorised the use of the VENTANA PTEN (SP218) diagnostic assay to identify patients with PTEN-deficient tumours who may be eligible for the therapy.

key_facts.fact: Approval is based on the 1,012-patient CAPItello-281 trial, in which adding capivasertib reduced the risk of progression or death by 19%.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is based on the CAPItello-281 trial of 1,012 patients: adding capivasertib to abiraterone and androgen deprivation therapy reduced the risk of progression or death by 19%, while median radiographic progression-free survival increased by 7.5 months (33.2 vs. 25.7 months).

stories.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.5-3.75% in Warsh debut; dot plot now sees rate hikes ahead

key_facts.fact: FOMC voted 12-0 to maintain the federal funds rate target range at 3.5%-3.75% on June 17, the first meeting led by new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 12 - 0 vote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.

key_facts.fact: The Fed cited elevated inflation tied in part to supply shocks including energy from the Middle East conflict; productivity and capital investment remain strong.
key_facts.excerpt: Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East... Inflation remains elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy.

key_facts.fact: New dot plot shows nine of 18 voting members projecting at least one rate hike before year-end, with six projecting two 25-basis-point hikes.
key_facts.excerpt: The FOMC also released a summary of economic projections, also known as the dot plot, which showed that nine of the 18 voting members project an interest rate hike before the end of 2026, with six projecting two 25-basis-point hikes.

key_facts.fact: Median projections see PCE inflation at 3.6% at year-end (up from 2.7% in March), real GDP at 2.2% (down from 2.4%), and unemployment at 4.3%.
key_facts.excerpt: median projections, real GDP rises at 2.2 percent this year, 2.3 percent next year, and total PCE inflation runs at 3.6 percent this year, 2.3 percent next year. The unemployment rate stands at about 4.3 percent.

key_facts.fact: After the decision, CME FedWatch showed odds of rates staying at 3.5-3.75% through year-end fell to 14.2% from 40.3% a day earlier, with markets repricing toward a December hike.
key_facts.excerpt: The CME FedWatch tool shows a 14.2% chance that rates will remain at their current range of 3.5% to 3.75% through the end of this year, down from 40.3% a day ago.

stories.headline: Nvidia unveils ENPIRE: AI coding agents autonomously run robot training to 99% success without humans

key_facts.fact: Nvidia, Carnegie Mellon and UC Berkeley released ENPIRE, a closed-loop framework that lets AI coding agents reset physical scenes, run hardware trials, verify outcomes and rewrite policy code without human intervention between iterations
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers from NVIDIA's GEAR Lab, Carnegie Mellon University, and UC Berkeley today released ENPIRE— a closed-loop framework that hands the entire robotics research cycle to AI coding agents: resetting physical scenes, running hardware trials, verifying outcomes, and rewriting code until a policy works. No human required between iterations.

key_facts.fact: ENPIRE deployed 8 Codex coding agents on a fleet of 8 dual-arm YAM robot stations, each with its own hardware, GPU and token budget; agents coordinate by sharing code through Git
key_facts.excerpt: ENPIRE scales to a full fleet: eight dual-arm YAM robot stations, each with its own hardware, computer, and coding agent. The agents test different hypotheses at the same time and share results only through Git, the standard version control tool for software.

key_facts.fact: Agents reached 99% success on dexterous tasks including organizing pins into a pin box, seating GPUs and cutting zip ties
key_facts.excerpt: Powered by ENPIRE, frontier coding agents can autonomously develop a policy to achieve a 99% success rate on challenging, dexterous manipulation tasks in the real world, such as PushT, organizing pins into a pin box, and using a cutter to cut a zip tie.

key_facts.fact: The system has 4 modules: Environment (auto-reset and verification), Policy Improvement, Rollout (parallel hardware trials), and Evolution (agents read research papers and revise training code)
key_facts.excerpt: We introduce ENPIRE, a harness framework for coding agents that instantiates this physical feedback routine with four core modules: an Environment module (EN) for automatic reset and verification, a Policy Improvement module (PI) that launches policy refinement, a Rollout module (R) to evaluate policies with single or multiple physical robots operating in parallel, and an Evolution module (E) in which coding agents analyze logs, consult literature, improve training infrastructure and algorithm code to address failure modes.

key_facts.fact: The release coincided with Jensen Huang's VivaTech 2026 keynote in Paris, which featured physical AI as its central theme
key_facts.excerpt: As Jensen Huang addresses a packed hall at VivaTech 2026 in Paris today with physical AI as his central theme, the NVIDIA research lab behind his bolder claims just published the most concrete evidence yet of what that thesis looks like on real hardware.

stories.headline: French silicon-qubit startup Quobly raises €115M Series A to commercialize quantum on 300mm wafers

key_facts.fact: Quobly, spun out of France's CEA-Leti, raised €115 million in Series A funding to accelerate commercial development of silicon-based quantum computers, the company announced June 17.
key_facts.excerpt: Quobly has raised €115m for silicon quantum computing systems development. The funding supports 300mm wafer processes, FD-SOI technology, and a full-stack architecture spanning qubits, control electronics, and software.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Bpifrance, Swiss security-chip maker SEALSQ, and STMicroelectronics, with participation from the European Innovation Council Fund, Blast, ALIAD (Air Liquide's venture arm), and Innovacom; existing shareholders include CEA, CNRS, Quantonation, and Supernova Invest.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing was led by Bpifrance, the Swiss security-chip maker SEALSQ and STMicroelectronics, with the European Innovation Council, Blast, Air Liquide's venture arm ALIAD and Innovacom also taking part.

key_facts.fact: Quobly's approach builds qubits on the same 300-millimetre silicon wafers used by commercial chip fabs, leveraging FD-SOI technology and existing semiconductor supply chains rather than superconducting or trapped-ion designs.
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than the superconducting or trapped-ion designs that dominate the field, Quobly builds qubits on the same 300-millimetre silicon wafers that already run through commercial chip fabs, a bet that quantum hardware can ride the existing semiconductor supply chain instead of replacing it.

stories.headline: Sanders unveils American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act: 50% stock tax to seed ~$7T public fund

key_facts.fact: Senator Bernie Sanders shared the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act first to the AP on June 17, formalizing a previous proposal into legislation.
key_facts.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — As artificial intelligence companies reshape the economy and race toward trillion-dollar valuations, Sen. Bernie Sanders is proposing a sweeping transfer of wealth and power from the industry to the American public... The legislation, shown first to The Associated Press, would create a sovereign wealth fund overseen by an independent commission and financed through a one-time 50% tax on the stock of the largest AI companies.

key_facts.fact: The bill would impose a one-time 50% stock tax (not cash) on AI companies that reach $200M in annual AI sales, including OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI.
key_facts.excerpt: The 50% tax would apply to AI companies that reach $200 million in annual AI sales. Any new AI company that reaches that benchmark would also be subject to the tax... Unlike a traditional tax, the proposal would require companies to transfer stock rather than cash, effectively making the American public a major shareholder in the country's largest AI firms.

key_facts.fact: Sanders estimates the fund would reach about $7 trillion and generate hundreds of billions annually for direct payments to Americans plus health, education and housing programs.
key_facts.excerpt: Sanders estimates that the tax would create a nearly $7 trillion fund that would generate hundreds of billions of dollars annually in direct payments to Americans and programs such as health care, education and housing.

key_facts.fact: A seven-person commission, nominated by the President and confirmed by the Senate, would manage the fund and exercise voting rights to block decisions harmful to the public.
key_facts.excerpt: A seven-person independent commission — nominated by the president and confirmed by the Senate — would manage the fund and use its voting shares 'to block decisions that hurt the American people and to push for policies that help them,' the bill summary says.

key_facts.fact: A proposed 5% annual fund dividend would deliver direct payments of more than $1,000 to every American.
key_facts.excerpt: Sanders proposes that a 5% annual dividend from the fund would provide direct payments of more than $1,000 to every American. If companies grow, the gains would be used for public goods such as education, housing and health care.

stories.headline: Trump announces Apple-Intel chip manufacturing deal; Intel stock jumps 9% premarket

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump said on Truth Social on June 18 that Apple had agreed to work with Intel to design and build its chips in the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post on Thursday that Apple had agreed to work with Intel to design and build its chips in the United States.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares jumped roughly 9% in premarket trading after the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel stock jumped roughly 9% in premarket trading after President Donald Trump announced that Apple will collaborate with the chipmaker on domestic semiconductor design and manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: The deal helps Apple diversify away from heavy reliance on TSMC, whose advanced production lines are in high demand from AI chipmakers like Nvidia and AMD.
key_facts.excerpt: A partnership with Intel helps Apple diversify its manufacturing base as it seeks additional chip capacity. The iPhone maker relies heavily on TSMC, whose advanced production lines are in high demand from AI chipmakers such as Nvidia and AMD.

key_facts.fact: Intel announced on June 16-17 at the VLSI Symposium in Honolulu that its 18A-P process node had entered risk production, an early proving stage.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel announced it's making the new chip node, 18A-P, at the VLSI Symposium in Honolulu, Hawaii, on Tuesday. First announced last year, 18A-P is now in what's known as 'risk production,' an early production stage with data indicating it will meet customer requirements upon final qualification.

key_facts.fact: Trump framed the agreement as the third major foundry customer win his administration has personally announced for Intel this year, following Nvidia and Tesla's TerraFab.
key_facts.excerpt: This is now the third major foundry customer win Trump has personally announced for Intel this year, following Nvidia and Tesla's TerraFab. Trump's framing was explicit about his administration's direct role: 'We decided to help Intel in exchange for 10% of their shares...'

key_facts.fact: Neither company has confirmed specifics on which Apple chip lines would be made by Intel, what process node, or volume.
key_facts.excerpt: The specifics remain genuinely unclear. Bloomberg had reported last month that Apple was considering Intel and Samsung's U.S. foundries to produce certain main processors powering its devices — but no confirmation exists yet on which specific Apple chip lines would move to Intel manufacturing, what node would be used, or what volume is involved.

stories.headline: Trump confirms Apple will work with Intel to design and build chips in US; Intel jumps ~9% premarket

key_facts.fact: On June 18 Truth Social, Trump said Apple agreed to work with Intel to design and build its chips in the United States; Intel shares jumped about 9% in premarket trading.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel stock jumped roughly 9% in premarket trading after President Donald Trump announced that Apple will collaborate with the chipmaker on domestic semiconductor design and manufacturing. Trump made the announcement on Truth Social on June 18, framing the partnership as a win for American manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Trump's post specifically said: 'Apple has agreed to work with Intel to design and build its Chips in America.' Apple shares gained 0.6%.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Apple has agreed to work with Intel to design and build its Chips in America,' Trump said in a Truth Social post in the early hours on Thursday. Apple shares gained 0.6%.

key_facts.fact: Apple is Intel's third major foundry win after Nvidia and Elon Musk's TeraFab, with Trump claiming credit for brokering all three.
key_facts.excerpt: 'First, we helped bring in Nvidia, and they agreed to build their first level Chips with Intel. Next, Elon agreed to build his TerraFab, the largest Chip Factory in the World, designed together with Intel's Technology team,' he wrote.

key_facts.fact: Apple ditched Intel processors in 2020 for in-house Arm designs fabbed by TSMC; the new deal positions Intel Foundry as production partner for Apple-designed chips, not a return to Intel CPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple famously ditched Intel's processors in 2020, transitioning its Mac lineup to custom-designed silicon built on Arm architecture and manufactured by Taiwan's TSMC. The new collaboration doesn't necessarily mean Apple is going back to Intel-designed chips. Instead, Intel appears to be positioning its foundry services as the production partner for chips that Apple designs in-house.

key_facts.fact: The U.S. government took a 10% stake in Intel last year for roughly $10B; that position has grown to be worth more than $50B.
key_facts.excerpt: Last year, the Trump administration took a 10% stake in Intel and announced plans to invest roughly $10 billion in the chipmaker to build or expand U.S. factories. Trump previously said he 'should have asked for more' of a stake in Intel, eight months after the government's Intel position grew to be worth more than $50 billion.
